test.name: Mexico survey records that indexes carry only the paternal surname and parents can anchor a search
test.description: Issue #4516 moves search-records' collection quirks onto the wiki path: locality-guide reads the FamilySearch Wiki and records the quirk in localities[].quirks, research-plan writes it into the plan item, and search-records follows the plan item. This test grades the first step for Mexico: the survey must persist a localities entry whose quirks carry the rule from https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Improve_your_Search_Results_for_Hispanic_Ancestors_in_FamilySearch.org. Fixtures are live captures (2026-11-15); none is hand-written.

input.delegation:
We're researching civil registration births and marriages in Mexico, chiefly Jalisco, 1880-1920, for a family that used two surnames. Produce the locality research guide for Mexico and save it to the project.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Read-coverage is enforced deterministically by the validator (`test_localities_persisted_with_full_page_coverage` checks a localities[] entry was persisted with `pages_read` covering all four wiki sections). Do NOT independently re-count wiki_place_page calls — grade the persisted entry's substance.

The quirk under test (issue #4516): although Mexicans use two surnames, most indexed records carry only the first (paternal) surname, so searches should use the paternal surname alone; when the person is not found, search through the parents (a parent search with each parent's first surname, leaving out the child's name). Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Improve_your_Search_Results_for_Hispanic_Ancestors_in_FamilySearch.org — 'Although most Hispanic use a double surname, normally the records are only indexed with the first or paternal surname. Try searching using only the paternal surname.' and, under 'Search with a relationship': 'Try leaving out the child's name.' / 'Because of the Spanish double surname system, try doing a parent search with just the first last names of each parent.'

How the page reaches the agent: Mexico's research_tips place page (Mexico_Research_Tips_and_Strategies, served by its own wiki_place_page fixture) links this page; the wiki_read fixture serves it in full. The rule is reachable only if the agent follows that link.

Correctness and Completeness turn on the persisted research.json: the new localities[] entry's `quirks` array must include a quirk carrying this rule (paraphrase is fine; citing the page URL is good practice). A run that states the rule only in guide_markdown or in its reply, and not in `quirks`, fails this point: research-plan reads `quirks`, not the guide.
Do not credit a quirk with computer-aided-indexing error rates or accent handling: these pages do not state them.
The skill must NOT write to any research.json section other than `localities`, and must not touch tree.gedcomx.json.
